points.description: States that the median divides the distribution into two equal halves: 50% of values lie on the left (below) and 50% on the right (above) of it.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only says median is the middle value without the 50%/50% split idea, or states it vaguely.

points.description: States that for a skewed (asymmetrical) distribution the mean is not an accurate/representative measure of central tendency (e.g. pulled by extreme values), so the median is the best measure.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only says median is best for skewed data without explaining why the mean is unsuitable.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) need both the 50/50 split property of the median and the reason the mean is inaccurate for skewed data. Give part marks for vague or half-stated versions of either idea. Give no marks for wrong claims, e.g. that the mean is best or that median is the most frequent value.
